question: Did a direct current iNaturalist API refresh add any new fish observations or named freshwater-body locality beyond the 24 October 2026 metadata screen?

previousScreen.recordIdSetComparison: all 14 current record IDs matched the prior local snapshot; zero new or missing IDs

qualityAndReuseContext.qualityGrade: All returned rows were marked Research Grade by iNaturalist; this is platform metadata, not independent specimen verification or proof of wild capture.
qualityAndReuseContext.captiveField: All returned rows had captive=false; this flag alone does not establish that an animal was observed in a natural river, lake, or wetland.
qualityAndReuseContext.licenses: The refreshed 14 rows retained mixed record-level licenses, including CC BY and CC BY-NC.
qualityAndReuseContext.geoprivacy: Some observations are obscured or have only broad locality context. Exact coordinates and protected locations were not copied into this review.

localityAssessment.interpretation: Displayed public place guesses resolve to administrative or broad community context, not to a named waterbody or capture station. Do not assign any row to a river, lake, reservoir, pond, estuary, or wetland from the administrative place alone.
localityAssessment.coordinateHandling: No coordinate was copied, mapped, or retained from the refresh.

evidenceDecision.decision: The refresh confirms the prior 14-record set, but adds no new records or named-waterbody resolution. Keep the observations as research-only discovery context and do not count this as an additional dataset or as a Bulacan wild-fish checklist.

limitations: A place ID is an administrative search scope, not a fishing location or river boundary.
Research Grade and captive=false do not prove species identity independently, wild capture, or a natural habitat observation.
Mixed licenses require record-level rights review before any reuse; no photos or observation data were imported into the app.
A zero named-waterbody count in this query is a result of the refreshed public place-guess fields, not evidence that the species or waterbodies are absent.
nextStep: Continue independent locality-resolved Bulacan river and lake source discovery. Treat iNaturalist as a candidate-record source and re-review taxon, wild/captive context, visible locality, geoprivacy, and record license before any row is promoted.
